name: Ladder (dip-buyer), 1-hour BTC
one_liner: Buys Bitcoin when it dips 8, 16 or 24 percent below its recent highest price, sells when it bounces +5%, stops if it keeps falling −10%, and after a win waits for a small 0.75% dip to buy again. It only trades while the market is calm.
how_it_works: Think of a person waiting at a staircase hoping for bounces. Three steps below the recent high: if price falls to step 1 it buys; if it keeps falling it buys at steps 2 and 3 too (this is called averaging down). Each buy waits for a +5% bounce to sell; if price instead falls 10% from that buy, it sells to limit the damage. When a trade wins and sells, it waits for a small dip and buys again, recycling the same money.

params.name: When it buys
params.plain: When price falls to 8%, 16% or 24% below the highest price of the last ~12 days. Each is a separate order with its own money.
params.why: Three buy steps = three chances, but also three amounts of money at risk at once.

params.name: When it sells (profit)
params.why: A fixed, small goal: +5% before the stop. This is the 'reward' of the trade.

params.name: When it cuts losses (stop)
params.why: The 'brake': if a buy keeps falling, it accepts −10% instead of an unknown bigger loss.

params.name: Buy again after a win
params.plain: After a profitable sell, it waits for a 0.75% dip and buys again with the same money.
params.why: Recycles the money so one lot of capital can trade many cycles.

params.name: Only in calm markets
params.plain: It compares the average price of the last 50 candles with the average of the last 100. If they drift apart more than 0.2%, it treats it as a 'trend' and does nothing. It only trades again when they are nearly together.
params.why: This strategy makes money when prices go back and forth. In a one-way trend, 'buy the dip' keeps buying a falling knife — so it refuses to trade in trends.

params.name: Why this page exists
params.plain: Your original idea, made wide and careful.
params.why: It shows how little a careful dip-buying ladder trades (33 rounds in 4 years) and that it still loses (profit factor 0.62).
